newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool prices fall further in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool prices fall further in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices fell sharply early this week, but falls eased on the last day's sales in Sydney and Adelaide, pastoral group Wesfarmers Dalgety said.
The eastern market indicator fell by seven cents to 598 cents a kg clean. Of the 69,857 bales on offered, the trade bought 87.4 percent and the pass-in rate was 12.6 percent.
Trade competition was led by Japanese and Chinese buyers with support from local buyers and most sectors of the trade.
The Australian Council of Wool Exporters said the further easing in prices was seen as an additional small correction to the unsustainable rise that occurred earlier this month.
"Market sentiment was positive at the close of sales," the council said.
Wool International said its stockpile of unsold wool totalled 1,889,771 as at January 30.
In the futures market, a total of 139 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended January 30.
Sales next week are in Goulburn, Melbourne and Fremantle with a total of 110,700 bales rostered for sale.
